QuestionStmt.S: If maximum energy is stored in a capacitor at $t = 0$ then the time after which, current in the circuit will be maximum is

Solution.S:
At $t=0$, charge is maximum: $q = q_0 \cos\omega_0 t$.

Current $i = \frac{dq}{dt} = q_0\omega_0 \sin\omega_0 t = i_0 \sin\omega_0 t$.

Current is maximum when $\sin\omega_0 t = 1 \Rightarrow \omega_0 t = \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t = \frac{\pi}{2\omega_0}$.

$\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{16 \times 10^{-3} \times 10 \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{16 \times 10^{-8}}} = \frac{1}{4 \times 10^{-4}} = 2500$ rad/s.

$t = \frac{\pi}{2 \times 2500} = \frac{\pi}{5000} = 2\pi \times 10^{-4}$ s.

Thus the correct option is C.
